lessons.titleEn: sit tight and hope for the best
lessons.titleZh: 耐心等候，盼望有好結果

target.pattern: \b(?:sit tight and hope|sits tight and hopes|sat tight and hoped|sitting tight and hoping) for the best\b

brief.meaningEn: Wait patiently after doing what one can, while remaining uncertain about the outcome.
brief.meaningZh: 完成自己能做的事後，因結果尚未確定而耐心等待，盼望有好結果。
brief.grammar: sit tight and hope for the best; sat is the past form of sit.
brief.register: Informal conversational language. An applicant might say it to a friend after sending a completed application.
brief.boundaryZh: 重點是暫時無法再左右結果時等待；不應用來代替仍有責任完成的工作。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是保證成功，也不是故意忽略可採取的補救行動。
brief.outcomeZh: 能分辨已盡力後等待與未完成工作便被動寄望。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 97, row 5; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: After the interview, we could only sit tight and hope for the best.
sources.expression: sit tight and hope for the best

notes: AI-authored provisional draft; independent reviews remain pending.

listening.promptZh: 講者送出申請後打算怎樣做？

options.en: Wait for the decision because no further action is currently required.
options.zh: 暫時無需再採取行動，等待決定。

options.en: Rewrite the application before the announced deadline.
options.zh: 在公布的截止日期前重寫申請。

options.en: Call the office every hour to demand a result.
options.zh: 每小時致電辦事處催促結果。

options.en: Assume the place has already been confirmed.
options.zh: 假設名額已獲確認。

listening.explanationZh: 材料已送齊，辦事處會下星期回覆；現在只能耐心等候。
listening.en: I sent the completed application and all the documents yesterday. The office said it would reply next week, so for now I can only sit tight and hope for the best.
listening.zh: 我昨天已送出完整申請和所有文件。辦事處說下星期會回覆，所以目前我只能耐心等候，盼望有好結果。

reply.promptEn: We have submitted every document and the decision comes next week. What can we do now?
reply.promptZh: （我們已提交所有文件，下星期才有決定。現在可以做甚麼？）

options.en: Wait for the announced reply before chasing the office.
options.zh: 等到公布的回覆時間再向辦事處查詢。

options.en: Keep a copy of the submitted documents while waiting.
options.zh: 等候期間保留已提交文件的副本。

options.en: We can sit tight and hope for the best until the office responds.
options.zh: 辦事處回覆前，我們只能耐心等候，盼望好結果。

options.en: Plan what to do if the answer is yes or no.
options.zh: 先計劃獲批及不獲批時的下一步。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都是提交後可行的做法；金句點出結果未定而暫時等待。

scene.promptZh: 樂團已完成試音，評審說周五才公布名單，也沒有補交材料的安排。團員現在只能等。哪句最貼切？

options.en: They must sit tight and hope for the best until Friday.
options.zh: 他們只能耐心等到周五，盼望有好結果。

options.en: They should submit the recording they have not yet finished.
options.zh: 他們應提交尚未完成的錄音。

options.en: They have already secured a place and can announce it now.
options.zh: 他們已獲得名額，可以現在宣布。

scene.explanationZh: 試音已完成，結果未定且暫無下一步，適合耐心等候。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況仍有必要行動，不能只說 sit tight and hope for the best？

options.en: The applicant has not sent the required reference before today’s deadline.
options.zh: 申請人尚未在今天截止前送出必需的推薦信。

options.en: The complete application is under review until next week.
options.zh: 完整申請正在審核，下星期才有結果。

options.en: The interview is over and the panel has given a decision date.
options.zh: 面試已結束，評審團已說明公布日期。

contrast.explanationZh: 仍欠必需文件且今天截止，應先完成行動。

dialogue.promptZh: （甲：我們昨天送出修訂方案，資助方說星期一才決定。還有甚麼要提交嗎？乙：______）

options.en: No; we can sit tight and hope for the best until Monday.
options.zh: 不用；星期一前我們可以耐心等候，盼望好結果。

options.en: Keep the submitted version ready in case the funder has a question.
options.zh: 保留已提交的版本，以便資助方有疑問時查閱。

options.en: Check that the funder has our current contact details.
options.zh: 檢查資助方是否有我們最新的聯絡資料。

dialogue.explanationZh: 材料已提交且有回覆日期，金句表達目前只能等候。
dialogue.promptEn: A: We sent the revised proposal yesterday, and the funder said it will decide on Monday. Is there anything left to submit? B: ______

speaking.en: We have sent the final design to the judges, so we will sit tight and hope for the best until the results come out.
speaking.zh: 我們已把最終設計交給評判，所以公布結果前會耐心等候，盼望有好結果。
speaking.promptZh: 說明已完成的步驟及尚待公布的結果。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：團體已交齊必要資料，審核機構仍未公布結果，暫時沒有其他必需步驟。用英文交代已完成甚麼、等待甚麼。
writing.selfCheckZh: 須明確說明已盡力及結果未定；不要把未交文件的情況寫成只能等候。

examples.en: After the grant panel confirmed it had every form, the youth group decided to sit tight and hope for the best until the decision arrived.
examples.zh: 資助評審小組確認收齊所有表格後，青年團體決定耐心等候，盼望決定有好結果。

examples.en: The bakery had submitted its permit application and could only sit tight and hope for the best while the council reviewed it.
examples.zh: 麵包店已提交許可證申請；議會審核期間，店方只能耐心等候，盼望有好結果。

takeaways.en: After completing the application, we may sit tight and hope for the best.
takeaways.zh: 完成申請後，我們或只能耐心等候，盼望好結果。

takeaways.en: Do the required work first; only then sit tight and hope for the best.
takeaways.zh: 先完成必需工作，然後才耐心等候，盼望好結果。

lessons.titleZh: 壓住怒氣；不讓情緒爆發

brief.meaningEn: Control an emotion, especially irritation, so it is not expressed in an outburst.
brief.meaningZh: 控制情緒，尤其是怒氣，避免當場爆發。
brief.grammar: keep a lid on it; it needs a clear emotion antecedent in context.
brief.register: Informal conversational language. A colleague may say it to a friend after managing irritation during a meeting.
brief.boundaryZh: 指情緒存在但被克制，不等於沒有不滿，也不是掩蓋必須報告的事實；與 keep a cool head 側重清晰判斷的用法不同。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是蓋上真正的蓋子；不能在沒有情緒所指的語境中任意使用 it。
brief.outcomeZh: 能辨別克制怒氣與沒有怒氣、或當場爆發。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 98, row 2; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: He was irritated but managed to keep a lid on it.

notes: AI-authored provisional draft; independent reviews remain pending.

listening.promptZh: 講者在會議中怎樣處理自己的怒氣？

options.en: The speaker felt irritated but answered calmly rather than shouting.
options.zh: 講者感到煩躁，但仍平靜回答，沒有叫嚷。

options.en: The speaker had no strong feeling about the interruption.
options.zh: 講者對打斷毫無強烈感受。

options.en: The speaker shouted until the meeting stopped.
options.zh: 講者一直叫嚷，直到會議停止。

options.en: The speaker left without answering any question.
options.zh: 講者沒有回答問題便離開。

listening.explanationZh: 講者確實生氣，但控制住，平靜回答。
listening.en: I was irritated when Ken interrupted me again, but I managed to keep a lid on it. I answered the question calmly and asked to finish my point.
listening.zh: Ken 再次打斷我時，我很煩躁，但設法壓住怒氣。我平靜回答問題，並請他讓我說完。

reply.promptEn: Ken keeps interrupting you in the meeting. How can you respond without snapping?
reply.promptZh: （Ken 在會議中不斷打斷你。你怎樣回應才不會發火？）

options.en: Ask calmly for a chance to finish your point.
options.zh: 平靜地請他讓你說完。

options.en: Pause before replying so you can choose your words.
options.zh: 回應前先停一停，想清楚用詞。

options.en: I am annoyed, but I will keep a lid on it and address the interruption directly.
options.zh: 我很惱火，但會壓住怒氣，直接處理被打斷的問題。

options.en: Suggest a turn-taking rule for the rest of the meeting.
options.zh: 建議餘下會議輪流發言。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都能控制衝突；金句點明有怒氣但克制住。

scene.promptZh: 球員對裁判的判決很惱火，卻沒有吼叫，而是深呼吸後平靜地請隊長提出疑問。哪句最貼切？

options.en: The player kept a lid on it despite feeling angry.
options.zh: 球員雖然生氣，仍壓住怒氣。

options.en: The player felt no frustration with the decision.
options.zh: 球員對判決毫無不滿。

options.en: The player shouted at the referee before calming down.
options.zh: 球員先向裁判吼叫，之後才平靜。

scene.explanationZh: 怒氣存在，卻沒有當場爆發。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況未能說當事人 keep a lid on it？

options.en: She yelled at her colleague and slammed the door in anger.
options.zh: 她憤怒地向同事吼叫，並用力關門。

options.en: She was annoyed but waited until after the meeting to raise it calmly.
options.zh: 她很惱火，但等到會後才平靜提出。

options.en: She felt angry and took a breath before responding.
options.zh: 她感到生氣，先深呼吸才回答。

contrast.explanationZh: 怒氣已明顯爆發，與克制情緒相反。

dialogue.promptZh: （甲：供應商責怪我們時，我非常憤怒，但仍禮貌回答，並要求查看紀錄。乙：______）

options.en: You kept a lid on it while still asking for the facts.
options.zh: 你壓住了怒氣，同時仍要求查明事實。

options.en: You asked for the records before deciding who was responsible.
options.zh: 你在決定責任誰屬前先要求看紀錄。

options.en: You stayed in the conversation instead of leaving immediately.
options.zh: 你留在對話中，沒有立即離開。

dialogue.explanationZh: 金句特別指出有怒氣但控制住，不妨礙查清事實。
dialogue.promptEn: A: I was furious when the supplier blamed us, but I answered politely and asked for the records. B: ______

speaking.en: I was annoyed by the delay, but I kept a lid on it and asked the receptionist for an updated time.
speaking.zh: 延誤令我惱火，但我壓住怒氣，向接待員查詢更新時間。
speaking.promptZh: 說明感受、克制行為和實際詢問。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：某人對工作失誤或服務問題感到生氣，卻克制住，改以平靜方式處理。用英文交代怒氣、克制及後續行動。
writing.selfCheckZh: it 要有明確情緒所指；不能寫成當事人完全沒有怒氣。

examples.en: The stage manager was furious about the missed cue, but she kept a lid on it and discussed the timing after rehearsal.
examples.zh: 舞台監督對錯過提示非常生氣，但她壓住怒氣，在綵排後才討論時間安排。

examples.en: When the bus left early, Omar felt irritated; he kept a lid on it and calmly asked the driver about the next service.
examples.zh: 巴士提早開走時，Omar 感到煩躁；他壓住怒氣，平靜地向司機詢問下一班車。

takeaways.en: She kept a lid on it when irritation rose during the meeting.
takeaways.zh: 會議中怒氣上升時，她仍壓住情緒。

takeaways.en: He felt angry but chose to keep a lid on it and ask a clear question.
takeaways.zh: 他感到生氣，卻選擇壓住怒氣，提出清楚問題。

brief.meaningEn: Repeatedly irritate many people, often through an ongoing behaviour or inconvenience.
brief.meaningZh: 因反覆行為或持續不便而惹得許多人心煩。
brief.grammar: get on someone’s nerves; with singular subject, gets. Apostrophe may be straight or curly.
brief.register: Informal conversational language. A passenger may say it to another passenger about repeated announcements or delays.
brief.boundaryZh: 指持續或反覆的煩擾；不等於一次嚴重傷害，也不是每個人都必然真的同意。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是碰到神經的字面意思；everybody/everyone 會是概括說法，避免無憑據地斷言每個人都生氣。
brief.outcomeZh: 能根據反覆跡象描述群體煩躁。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 98, row 4; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: A long delay gets on everyone's nerves.

notes: AI-authored provisional draft; independent reviews remain pending.

listening.promptZh: 月台上的人為甚麼越來越煩躁？

options.en: The same loud warning has repeated every few minutes for an hour.
options.zh: 同一段大聲警告一小時內每隔幾分鐘就重播。

options.en: One brief safety notice was played at the start.
options.zh: 開始時只播放了一段簡短安全通知。

options.en: The train arrived at the advertised time.
options.zh: 列車按公布時間到達。

options.en: The volume was reduced after the first warning.
options.zh: 第一次警告後音量已調低。

listening.explanationZh: 重複一小時的大聲警告形成持續煩擾。
listening.en: The same loud warning has played every few minutes for an hour. People on the platform keep looking up and complaining. It is getting on everyone’s nerves.
listening.zh: 同一段大聲警告一小時內每隔幾分鐘就播一次。月台上的人不斷抬頭，亦有人抱怨。這惹得大家越來越心煩。

reply.promptEn: The warning keeps playing loudly and passengers are complaining. What could staff do?
reply.promptZh: （警告一直大聲重播，乘客開始抱怨。職員可以怎樣做？）

options.en: Check whether the warning still needs to play so often.
options.zh: 檢查是否仍有需要播得那麼頻密。

options.en: Lower the volume if the safety message remains audible.
options.zh: 在安全訊息仍清晰可聞的情況下調低音量。

options.en: It is getting on everyone’s nerves; let us fix the repeated announcement.
options.zh: 重複廣播惹得大家心煩；把它處理好吧。

options.en: Tell passengers why the message is repeating and when it may stop.
options.zh: 向乘客解釋訊息為何重播，以及何時可能停止。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都可回應持續煩擾；金句使用目標片語。

scene.promptZh: 辦公室冷氣每隔兩分鐘發出尖銳聲響，同事一再停下工作並抱怨。哪句最貼切？

options.en: The recurring noise gets on everyone’s nerves.
options.zh: 反覆聲響惹得大家心煩。

options.en: One short sound helped workers notice the machine needed checking.
options.zh: 一次短聲響提醒員工機器需要檢查。

options.en: The workers continued without noticing any sound.
options.zh: 員工沒有留意聲響，照常工作。

scene.explanationZh: 聲響反覆出現，同事持續受煩擾。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況未見持續煩擾，較不適合說 gets on everyone’s nerves？

options.en: The host gives one brief reminder, and guests continue talking comfortably.
options.zh: 主持人作一次簡短提醒，賓客繼續自在交談。

options.en: A door alarm beeps repeatedly throughout the meeting.
options.zh: 門鈴警報整場會議反覆響起。

options.en: A colleague interrupts each speaker several times.
options.zh: 一名同事多次打斷每位發言者。

contrast.explanationZh: 一次簡短提醒後氣氛如常，未顯示反覆煩擾。

dialogue.promptZh: （甲：打印機每隔兩分鐘就發出尖銳聲響，大家一直問何時會停。乙：______）

options.en: That beep gets on everyone’s nerves; let us ask for a repair.
options.zh: 那聲響惹得大家心煩；找人維修吧。

options.en: We can check whether the printer displays an error code.
options.zh: 我們可以檢查打印機有沒有顯示錯誤代碼。

options.en: We could move urgent printing to the machine downstairs.
options.zh: 我們可以改用樓下機器處理急件。

dialogue.explanationZh: 金句概括反覆聲響造成的群體煩躁。
dialogue.promptEn: A: The printer makes that high-pitched beep every two minutes, and people keep asking when it will stop. B: ______

speaking.en: The repeated reminder got on everyone’s nerves because it interrupted every speaker during the rehearsal.
speaking.zh: 重複的提醒惹得大家心煩，因為綵排期間每位講者都被打斷。
speaking.promptZh: 指出反覆發生的煩擾及受影響的人。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：某個聲響或行為在一段時間內不斷重複，周圍的人表現出煩躁。用英文交代反覆來源及對大家的影響。
writing.selfCheckZh: 要有反覆煩擾與受影響的群體，不要把一次短暫提示誇大成人人心煩。

examples.en: The broken gate alarm gets on everyone’s nerves because it sounds every few minutes during the evening meal, and family members keep complaining about it.
examples.zh: 壞掉的大門警報器每隔幾分鐘就在晚飯期間響起，惹得大家心煩，家人亦反覆抱怨。

examples.en: At the studio, the repeated drilling got on everyone’s nerves; several artists complained that they could barely discuss their work.
examples.zh: 在工作室，反覆的鑽孔聲惹得大家心煩；幾名藝術家抱怨幾乎無法討論作品。

takeaways.en: A sound that repeats all evening can get on everyone’s nerves.
takeaways.zh: 整晚反覆的聲響可能惹得大家心煩。

takeaways.en: The long delay got on everyone’s nerves when no update arrived.
takeaways.zh: 久久沒有新消息，漫長延誤令大家心煩。

brief.meaningEn: Have an uncontrolled angry outburst, often in a childlike way.
brief.meaningZh: 以失控、帶點孩子氣的方式大發脾氣。
brief.grammar: throw a tantrum; threw is the past form.
brief.register: Informal and potentially judgemental. A supervisor may say it privately to a colleague about an adult shouting, but should describe behaviour precisely rather than use it to dismiss a legitimate complaint.
brief.boundaryZh: 指情緒失控的爆發，不等於任何強烈但有理據的投訴；使用時應避免把合理申訴污名化。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不只用於小孩，但形容成人時可能帶批評意味；不等於冷靜表達不滿。
brief.outcomeZh: 能分辨失控發脾氣與有理據地提出問題。

sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 98, row 6; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: Adults can complain without needing to throw a tantrum.

notes: AI-authored provisional draft; independent reviews remain pending.

listening.promptZh: 當事人對退款問題的反應有甚麼特點？

options.en: The customer shouted, stamped a foot and interrupted every reply.
options.zh: 顧客大聲叫嚷、跺腳，並打斷每個回答。

options.en: The person calmly explained the receipt discrepancy.
options.zh: 當事人平靜解釋收據差異。

options.en: The person asked one question and waited for an answer.
options.zh: 當事人問一條問題後等候回覆。

options.en: The person submitted a written complaint after the visit.
options.zh: 當事人在到訪後提交書面投訴。

listening.explanationZh: 大聲叫嚷、跺腳和不斷打斷，表現為失控的發脾氣。
listening.en: The refund delay was frustrating, but the customer began shouting, stamping a foot and interrupting every answer. He threw a tantrum instead of explaining the receipt problem calmly.
listening.zh: 退款延誤確實令人沮喪，但顧客開始叫嚷、跺腳，不斷打斷每個回答。他大發脾氣，沒有平靜說明收據問題。

reply.promptEn: The refund delay is real, but the customer is shouting and interrupting every answer. What should staff do?
reply.promptZh: （退款延誤確實存在，但顧客叫嚷並打斷每個回答。職員應怎樣做？）

options.en: Stay calm and explain the next refund step.
options.zh: 保持冷靜，說明下一個退款步驟。

options.en: Acknowledge the delay without accepting abusive behaviour.
options.zh: 承認延誤，同時不容忍辱罵行為。

options.en: He is throwing a tantrum; let us set a boundary and still check his receipt.
options.zh: 他正大發脾氣；我們設下界線，同時仍核對收據。

options.en: Offer to continue the discussion once everyone can speak safely.
options.zh: 待大家能安全交談時，提議繼續討論。

reply.explanationZh: 四句既處理真實退款問題，也回應失控行為；金句用目標片語描述爆發。

scene.promptZh: 球隊經理沒有讓一名成年人先上場；他當眾摔下隊服、吼叫，拒絕讓任何人說話。哪句最貼切？

options.en: He threw a tantrum when he did not get his way.
options.zh: 事情不如意時，他大發脾氣。

options.en: He calmly asked the manager for the selection criteria.
options.zh: 他平靜地向經理詢問選人準則。

options.en: He filed a reasoned complaint after the match.
options.zh: 他在賽後提出有理據的投訴。

scene.explanationZh: 當眾吼叫、摔衣服、打斷所有人，超出一般提出異議。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個做法有理據且受控制，未足以說 throw a tantrum？

options.en: She asks for a refund calmly and shows the incorrect charge.
options.zh: 她平靜要求退款，並出示錯誤收費。

options.en: She yells over every reply and kicks a chair.
options.zh: 她在每次回覆時都叫嚷，還踢椅子。

options.en: She shouts and refuses to hear the explanation.
options.zh: 她大聲叫嚷，不肯聽解釋。

contrast.explanationZh: 清楚提出證據和要求，不等於失控發脾氣。

dialogue.promptZh: （甲：他對延誤有合理不滿，但後來大聲叫嚷、撞翻椅子，也不讓任何人回答。乙：______）

options.en: He threw a tantrum, though the original complaint still needs an answer.
options.zh: 他大發脾氣，但原來的投訴仍需要處理。

options.en: We should document the delay and offer a clear response.
options.zh: 我們應記錄延誤，給予清楚回應。

options.en: We may need to pause the conversation until it is safe.
options.zh: 我們可能需要暫停交談，直到情況安全。

dialogue.explanationZh: 金句區分失控行為與仍須處理的合理投訴。
dialogue.promptEn: A: He had a valid complaint about the delay, but then he shouted, knocked over a chair and would not let anyone answer. B: ______

speaking.en: The guest threw a tantrum when the table was unavailable, but the staff still checked the reservation record.
speaking.zh: 沒有空桌時，賓客大發脾氣，但職員仍核對了訂位紀錄。
speaking.promptZh: 指出失控行為，同時保留實際問題。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：有人遇到真實不便或爭議，但反應變成叫嚷、摔東西或拒絕聆聽。用英文寫出起因及失控表現。
writing.selfCheckZh: 要有可觀察的失控行為；不要把冷靜、有理據的投訴寫成發脾氣。

examples.en: When the ticket machine rejected his card, Ben threw a tantrum, shouted at the attendant and refused to try another machine.
examples.zh: 售票機拒收 Ben 的卡時，他大發脾氣，向職員叫嚷，並拒絕試用另一部機器。

examples.en: The player threw a tantrum after a disputed call, slamming a racket down while the umpire tried to explain the decision.
examples.zh: 一項判決引起爭議後，球員大發脾氣，猛力摔下球拍，當時裁判正嘗試解釋決定。

takeaways.en: A valid complaint does not justify throwing a tantrum at staff.
takeaways.zh: 即使投訴有理，也不代表可向職員大發脾氣。

takeaways.en: He threw a tantrum by shouting and refusing to hear a reply.
takeaways.zh: 他叫嚷並拒絕聽回應，大發脾氣。

brief.meaningEn: Shaped mainly by what is easy or saves effort.
brief.meaningZh: 主要由方便或省力的考慮所主導。
brief.grammar: compound adjective convenience-driven before or after a noun; hyphenate before a noun.
brief.register: Neutral analytic wording. A researcher may use it to explain changing shopping behaviour to a colleague.
brief.boundaryZh: 指出方便是主要推力，不等於速度是唯一因素，亦不自動評論選擇好壞。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是「被迫購物」，也不是只要服務有網上平台便必然以方便為主導。
brief.outcomeZh: 能從選擇原因判斷方便是否主要驅動因素。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx

listening.promptZh: 講者認為顧客為甚麼改用新服務？

options.en: They chiefly value fewer steps and home delivery.
options.zh: 他們主要重視步驟較少和送貨上門。

options.en: They are required by law to use it.
options.zh: 法律規定他們必須使用。

options.en: They choose it chiefly for its traditional packaging.
options.zh: 他們主要因傳統包裝而選用。

options.en: They use it because the shop has no other products.
options.zh: 他們使用它是因為商店沒有其他產品。

listening.explanationZh: 顧客選擇的主要原因是省步驟和省交通時間。
listening.en: Customers still compare prices, but many now choose the service because ordering takes two taps and delivery comes to the door. Their shopping has become more convenience-driven.
listening.zh: 顧客仍會比較價格，但如今不少人選用這項服務，是因為只需按兩下就能下單，而且送貨上門。他們的購物行為變得更以方便為主導。

reply.promptEn: Why are customers using this service even though they still compare prices? Ordering takes two taps, and goods are delivered to their homes.
reply.promptZh: （顧客仍比較價格，但只需按兩下便可下單，貨品又送到家中。他們為甚麼選用這項服務？）

options.en: It saves them a separate trip to the shop.
options.zh: 這令他們不用專程到店。

options.en: They can place an order in just a couple of steps.
options.zh: 他們只需幾個步驟就能下單。

options.en: Their choice is increasingly convenience-driven because ordering and delivery are easy.
options.zh: 他們的選擇越來越以方便為主導，因為下單和收貨都容易。

options.en: Home delivery means they do not have to carry the goods back themselves.
options.zh: 送貨上門讓他們不用自己把貨品搬回家。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均解釋方便因素；金句用目標形容詞總結主要推力。

scene.promptZh: 學生仍關心課程質素，但報名時首先選可在手機上迅速完成申請的課程，而非填寫紙本表格的課程。哪句最貼切？

options.en: Their course search is becoming convenience-driven.
options.zh: 他們選課越來越以方便為主導。

options.en: Their choice is based solely on the teacher’s research record.
options.zh: 他們只按老師的研究紀錄選擇。

options.en: Their main aim is to collect printed forms.
options.zh: 他們的主要目的是收集紙本表格。

scene.explanationZh: 仍考慮質素，但選擇的首要因素是報名是否方便。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個決定的主要原因不是方便，較不宜稱為 convenience-driven？

options.en: She takes a slower route because she wants to support a local business.
options.zh: 她選較慢路線，因為想支持本地商戶。

options.en: He chooses a delivery option because it saves a trip.
options.zh: 他選送貨服務，因為不用專程出門。

options.en: They pick the app because it completes the task in two steps.
options.zh: 他們選用應用程式，因為兩步便可完成。

contrast.explanationZh: 主要動機是支持商戶，而非省時省力。

dialogue.promptZh: （甲：我們仍重視產品質素，但顧客如今選我們，是因為幾秒就能下單，而且可送貨上門。乙：______）

options.en: Their choices sound more convenience-driven than before.
options.zh: 他們的選擇聽起來比以前更以方便為主導。

options.en: We should keep checking whether product quality meets expectations.
options.zh: 我們應繼續檢查產品質素是否符合期望。

options.en: We can ask customers which part of delivery helps them most.
options.zh: 我們可以問顧客送貨安排哪部分最有幫助。

dialogue.explanationZh: 金句點出選擇的主要推力轉向方便。
dialogue.promptEn: A: We still care about product quality, but customers now choose us because ordering takes seconds and we deliver to their homes. B: ______

speaking.en: The library introduced self-service returns after noticing a convenience-driven shift toward shorter visits.
speaking.zh: 圖書館留意到訪客因求方便而傾向短暫到訪，於是推出自助還書服務。
speaking.promptZh: 說明方便如何主導某項選擇，不要假設質素完全不重要。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：某個機構發現顧客主要因省時間或少步驟而改變選擇。用英文指出選擇、方便因素及機構的回應。
writing.selfCheckZh: 明確說方便是主要動機；不要只因有網上服務便推斷所有顧客如此。

examples.en: The gym noticed convenience-driven membership choices: many users picked the branch with late opening hours near the station, so it added more evening slots there.
examples.zh: 健身室留意到會員選擇以方便為主導：許多會員選擇車站附近、營業至較晚的分店，因此健身室在那裏增設了晚間時段。

examples.en: A convenience-driven change led the pharmacy to offer online refills, because customers wanted to avoid an extra visit for routine medicine.
examples.zh: 以方便為主導的改變促使藥房提供網上續配，因為顧客希望避免為常用藥物多走一趟。

takeaways.en: Convenience-driven choices are shaped mainly by ease or saved effort.
takeaways.zh: 以方便為主導的選擇，主要受省事或省力影響。

takeaways.en: The new ordering service reflects convenience-driven shopping habits.
takeaways.zh: 新下單服務反映以方便為主導的購物習慣。

brief.meaningEn: Life experienced as moving at an uncomfortably rapid, relentless pace.
brief.meaningZh: 感覺生活以令人不適、停不下來的速度急速推進。
brief.grammar: life on fast-forward; fixed media-control metaphor, commonly feel like life on fast-forward.
brief.register: Informal reflective language. An employee may use it with a friend to describe constant alerts and rushed days.
brief.boundaryZh: 說主觀感到整體節奏太快，未必每件事真的加速；與單一次趕車或快速完成任務不同。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是影片真的快轉，也不是忙碌一定帶來興奮感。
brief.outcomeZh: 能區分持續急促的生活節奏與短暫繁忙。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 99, row 4; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: Constant alerts can make work feel like life on fast-forward.

notes: AI-authored provisional draft; independent reviews remain pending.

options.en: A relentless day of alerts and rushed tasks with little pause.
options.zh: 提醒和趕工接連不斷，幾乎沒有停頓的一天。

options.en: A single five-minute walk to catch a train.
options.zh: 為趕車而走快五分鐘。

options.en: A video played at double speed during a lesson.
options.zh: 課堂上以雙倍速度播放影片。

options.en: A quiet afternoon with no messages.
options.zh: 沒有訊息的安靜下午。

listening.explanationZh: 持續的提醒與趕工令整體生活節奏令人不適地加快。
listening.en: Messages arrived during breakfast, every meeting ran into the next, and I ate lunch while answering alerts. The whole day felt like life on fast-forward.
listening.zh: 早餐時就有訊息，會議一場接一場，我連吃午飯也在回覆提醒。整天感覺像生活被快轉。

reply.promptEn: My days are packed with alerts and meetings, and I barely pause for lunch. How can I describe the pace?
reply.promptZh: （每天提醒與會議排得滿滿，我連午餐也幾乎沒時間停下。可以怎樣形容節奏？）

options.en: The constant interruptions make the day feel rushed.
options.zh: 不斷被打斷，令整天顯得匆忙。

options.en: I move from one meeting to another without a proper break.
options.zh: 我一場會接一場，沒有像樣的休息。

options.en: It feels like life on fast-forward, with no time to slow down.
options.zh: 感覺像生活在快轉，完全沒時間慢下來。

options.en: The day rushes past before I can catch my breath.
options.zh: 整天匆忙地過去，我連喘口氣也來不及。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都能合理表達急促節奏；金句以目標比喻概括整體感受。

scene.promptZh: 護理員連續數星期接到夜間電話，白天又要趕往不同地點，連休息也被打斷。哪句最貼切？

options.en: The weeks felt like life on fast-forward for the carer.
options.zh: 那幾星期，護理員感覺生活像被快轉。

options.en: The carer hurried only once to catch a late bus.
options.zh: 護理員只為趕一班晚點巴士匆忙了一次。

options.en: The carer had a calm routine with regular breaks.
options.zh: 護理員的日常平靜，亦有固定休息。

scene.explanationZh: 連續數星期的急促節奏，符合對整體生活的比喻。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個例子只是短暫趕時間，未足以說 life on fast-forward？

options.en: He walks quickly for ten minutes to reach the cinema on time.
options.zh: 他快走十分鐘，準時到電影院。

options.en: For a month, she moves between shifts and messages without a break.
options.zh: 一個月內，她不斷應付輪班和訊息，沒有休息。

options.en: Every day feels packed with interruptions, deadlines and rushed meals.
options.zh: 每天都充滿打斷、截止日期和匆忙吃飯。

contrast.explanationZh: 單次快走不代表整體生活持續急促。

dialogue.promptZh: （甲：我早餐前就回覆提醒，在不同班次之間趕路，幾乎不記得上次安靜地過一個晚上是何時。乙：______）

options.en: That sounds like life on fast-forward; can you protect a regular break?
options.zh: 聽起來生活像在快轉；你能保留固定休息時間嗎？

options.en: You might list which alerts really need an immediate reply.
options.zh: 你可以列出哪些提醒真的需要即時回覆。

options.en: You could ask whether the shifts can be spaced out.
options.zh: 你可以問班次能否安排得疏一些。

dialogue.explanationZh: 金句概括持續急促的整體感受。
dialogue.promptEn: A: I answer alerts before breakfast, rush between shifts and barely remember when I last had a quiet evening. B: ______

speaking.en: Since the project began, my week has felt like life on fast-forward, with meetings, alerts and travel leaving almost no quiet time.
speaking.zh: 項目開始後，我這星期感覺生活像被快轉，會議、提醒和出行令我幾乎沒有安靜時間。
speaking.promptZh: 說出持續節奏與至少兩個使節奏加快的來源。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：某人連續多日被不同任務或提醒推着走，幾乎沒有喘息時間。用英文寫出持續時間、至少兩個壓力來源及整體感受。
writing.selfCheckZh: 必須呈現持續而令人疲憊的節奏；一次趕路不足以支持比喻。

examples.en: For the new parents, constant night waking and daytime appointments made the first month feel like life on fast-forward.
examples.zh: 對新手父母來說，夜間不斷醒來、日間又要赴約，令第一個月感覺生活像被快轉。

examples.en: During the festival week, rehearsals, deliveries and urgent calls made the organiser feel as if she were living life on fast-forward.
examples.zh: 節日期間，綵排、送貨和緊急來電接連不斷，令主辦人感覺自己活在快轉的生活中。

takeaways.en: Constant alerts can make a whole week feel like life on fast-forward.
takeaways.zh: 不斷的提醒可令整個星期感覺像生活被快轉。

takeaways.en: Life on fast-forward describes a sustained rush, not one hurried trip.
takeaways.zh: 快轉般的生活指持續匆忙，不是一次趕路。

brief.meaningEn: Gradually reduce people’s willingness to cooperate or their trust through repeated friction.
brief.meaningZh: 因反覆摩擦而逐漸削弱人們合作的意願或信任。
brief.grammar: drain goodwill; goodwill is uncountable, with no article.
brief.register: Neutral analytic language. A coordinator may say it to colleagues while reviewing repeated unclear rules.
brief.boundaryZh: 強調善意逐漸被耗損，不一定表示所有關係即時破裂；與一次普通分歧不同。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是抽走實際液體；善意不等於金錢儲備。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出反覆小問題如何削弱合作關係。

listening.promptZh: 講者擔心不斷更改值班表會帶來甚麼後果？

options.en: Volunteers may become less willing to cover extra shifts after repeated confusion.
options.zh: 義工反覆遇上混亂後，可能較不願代替別人值班。

options.en: Every volunteer will leave immediately today.
options.zh: 所有義工今天都會立即離開。

options.en: The noticeboard will run out of space.
options.zh: 告示板會沒有空間。

options.en: The event will need one extra chair.
options.zh: 活動需要多一張椅子。

listening.explanationZh: 反覆的規則變更和解釋不清，會逐步消耗義工善意。
listening.en: We have changed the volunteer rota three times without explaining why. People are still helping, but repeated confusion can drain goodwill and make them less willing to cover extra shifts.
listening.zh: 我們已三次更改義工值班表，卻沒有解釋原因。大家仍在幫忙，但反覆的混亂會消耗善意，令他們較不願意代替別人值班。

reply.promptEn: The volunteers still help, but we keep changing their shifts without explanation. What should we address?
reply.promptZh: （義工仍在幫忙，但我們不斷無解釋地更改班次。應處理甚麼？）

options.en: Explain why the latest change was needed.
options.zh: 解釋最新改動為何必要。

options.en: Ask volunteers which shifts are hardest to cover.
options.zh: 問義工哪些班次最難代替。

options.en: Repeated surprises can drain goodwill; let us agree on a stable process.
options.zh: 反覆的突發改動會消耗善意；訂立穩定流程吧。

options.en: Give people enough notice before any future change.
options.zh: 日後每次改動前，給大家足夠通知。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都能改善安排；金句點出反覆摩擦的長期合作代價。

scene.promptZh: 社區團隊每次都臨時改集合地點，居民仍會來，但越來越少人願意額外搬器材。哪句最貼切？

options.en: The repeated last-minute changes are draining goodwill.
options.zh: 反覆的臨時改動正在消耗善意。

options.en: One carefully explained change has increased trust.
options.zh: 一次解釋清楚的改動增加了信任。

options.en: Residents now volunteer for more tasks than before.
options.zh: 居民現在比以前更願意承擔額外工作。

scene.explanationZh: 居民未立即離開，但額外幫忙的意願逐漸下降。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況尚未見善意被逐漸消耗？

options.en: The organiser explains one unavoidable change early, and volunteers accept it.
options.zh: 主辦人及早解釋一次無可避免的改動，義工接受。

options.en: Repeated unexplained changes make helpers reluctant to return.
options.zh: 反覆且沒有解釋的改動令幫忙者不願回來。

options.en: Several broken promises leave partners less willing to cooperate.
options.zh: 多次失信令合作伙伴較不願協作。

contrast.explanationZh: 一次有解釋且被接受的改動，未顯示善意逐漸流失。

dialogue.promptZh: （甲：鄰居仍借器材給我們，但經過幾次臨時取消，每次我們再問，他們都猶豫。乙：______）

options.en: Those cancellations have drained goodwill; we need to give reliable notice.
options.zh: 那些取消安排消耗了善意；我們須提供可靠通知。

options.en: We could ask which dates work best before booking equipment.
options.zh: 我們可以在預訂器材前先問哪些日期最合適。

options.en: We should thank them for lending us equipment so far.
options.zh: 我們應感謝他們一直借出器材。

dialogue.explanationZh: 多次失信令鄰居漸漸不願幫忙，金句概括合作意願的流失。
dialogue.promptEn: A: The neighbours still lend us equipment, but after several late cancellations they hesitate whenever we ask. B: ______

speaking.en: Changing the plan every week drained goodwill among the organisers, even though most of them continued to help.
speaking.zh: 每週改變計劃消耗了主辦人之間的善意，儘管大多數人仍繼續幫忙。
speaking.promptZh: 說出反覆問題、合作意願如何變化，以及關係未必即時破裂。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：一個組織反覆失約或規則不清，合作者仍在參與，但額外幫忙的意願逐漸下降。用英文寫出反覆問題及信任的變化。
writing.selfCheckZh: 不要誇大成所有人即時離開；重點是善意逐步耗損。

examples.en: The club’s repeated late payments drained goodwill from the venue staff, who became reluctant to offer flexible hours.
examples.zh: 社團屢次遲付款消耗了場地職員的善意，令他們較不願意提供彈性時段。

examples.en: Unclear reimbursement rules drained goodwill in the parent group; members still volunteered, but fewer offered to buy supplies in advance.
examples.zh: 不清晰的報銷規則消耗了家長小組的善意；成員仍做義工，但較少人願意預先購買物資。

takeaways.en: Repeated broken promises can drain goodwill even before people stop helping.
takeaways.zh: 即使人們仍在幫忙，反覆失信也會消耗善意。

takeaways.en: The unclear rules drained goodwill and reduced volunteers’ willingness to cover extra shifts.
takeaways.zh: 不清晰規則消耗了善意，減少義工代班的意願。

brief.meaningEn: Become visibly angry or fail to remain calm when frustrated.
brief.meaningZh: 遇到挫折時失去冷靜，顯出怒氣。
brief.grammar: lose + possessive determiner + cool; lost is the past form.
brief.register: Informal conversational language. A person may use it about their own reaction to a friend after a frustrating change of plans.
brief.boundaryZh: 指冷靜開始失守；不要求大聲吼叫或摔東西。與 keep a lid on it 的克制怒氣相反，也較 throw a tantrum 的明顯失控爆發輕。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是體溫下降，也不等於任何短暫不滿都已發火。
brief.outcomeZh: 能分辨有怒氣、失去冷靜與激烈鬧脾氣。

sources.sentence: I try to avoid losing my cool when plans change.

listening.promptZh: 講者發現自己在改期時有甚麼反應？

options.en: The speaker’s voice grew sharp, so the speaker paused before continuing.
options.zh: 講者語氣變尖銳，於是先停一停才繼續。

options.en: The speaker remained completely relaxed throughout.
options.zh: 講者全程完全放鬆。

options.en: The speaker damaged the office furniture.
options.zh: 講者損壞辦公室家具。

options.en: The speaker had no opinion about the new time.
options.zh: 講者對新時間沒有看法。

listening.explanationZh: 語氣變尖銳表示開始失去冷靜，但及時暫停。
listening.en: When the appointment changed again, I felt my voice getting sharp. I was losing my cool, so I stopped for a moment before calling back.
listening.zh: 預約再次改期時，我察覺自己的語氣變得尖銳。我開始失去冷靜，所以先停一停才再致電。

reply.promptEn: The appointment changed again, and my voice is getting sharp. What should I do before calling back?
reply.promptZh: （預約又改期了，我的語氣開始變尖銳。再致電前應怎樣做？）

options.en: Take a short pause and decide what information you need.
options.zh: 先短暫停一停，想清楚需要甚麼資料。

options.en: Write down one clear question about the new appointment.
options.zh: 寫下一條關於新預約的清楚問題。

options.en: I am losing my cool; I should pause before I speak again.
options.zh: 我快失去冷靜；再次說話前應停一停。

options.en: Ask a colleague to help if you cannot speak calmly yet.
options.zh: 若仍無法平靜交談，請同事幫忙。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都能回復平靜；金句明確指出冷靜正在失守。

scene.promptZh: 客人得知火車再次延誤後，說話音量提高、語氣變尖銳，但仍能停下來聽職員解釋。哪句最貼切？

options.en: The passenger was losing his cool but had not stopped listening.
options.zh: 乘客開始失去冷靜，但仍願意聽解釋。

options.en: The passenger was entirely calm and showed no frustration.
options.zh: 乘客完全冷靜，沒有顯露不滿。

options.en: The passenger overturned a desk and refused all contact.
options.zh: 乘客推翻桌子，拒絕與人接觸。

scene.explanationZh: 語氣轉尖顯示開始發火，但尚未變成嚴重失控。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況只是感到不滿，尚未顯示有人 lose their cool？

options.en: She says the delay is frustrating in an even voice and asks for a new time.
options.zh: 她語氣平穩地說延誤令人沮喪，並查詢新時間。

options.en: He begins snapping at staff over minor questions.
options.zh: 他開始因小問題對職員惡言相向。

options.en: Her voice rises and she cuts off each reply.
options.zh: 她提高聲量，打斷每個回覆。

contrast.explanationZh: 有不滿但仍平穩溝通，未見冷靜失守。

dialogue.promptZh: （甲：取消安排令我不開心，我開始語氣尖銳，所以停下來深呼吸。乙：______）

options.en: You were losing your cool, and the pause helped you recover.
options.zh: 你當時快失去冷靜，而停一停幫你回復平靜。

options.en: You could ask for a new date after the call resumes.
options.zh: 通話恢復後，你可以詢問新日期。

options.en: You noticed a change in your voice before it became a bigger argument.
options.zh: 你留意到語氣變化，沒有讓事情演變成更大爭執。

dialogue.explanationZh: 金句準確命名冷靜失守及及時暫停。
dialogue.promptEn: A: I was upset about the cancellation and began speaking sharply, so I stopped and took a breath. B: ______

speaking.en: I was losing my cool when the bus was cancelled again, but I paused and asked for another route.
speaking.zh: 巴士再被取消時，我快失去冷靜，但仍停一停，改問其他路線。
speaking.promptZh: 說明令你生氣的事、冷靜失守跡象和調整行動。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：安排再次變動或錯誤重現，某人開始語氣尖銳，然後暫停或補救。用英文交代起因、失去冷靜的跡象和後續行動。
writing.selfCheckZh: 不要把平靜提出問題寫成發火，也不要把每次失去冷靜都誇大為摔東西。

examples.en: Mina realised she was losing her cool when the rehearsal time changed for the third time and her voice grew sharp, so she took a breath before replying.
examples.zh: 綵排時間第三次改動時，Mina 察覺自己的語氣變得尖銳、快失去冷靜，於是回覆前先深呼吸。

examples.en: After another billing error, the customer lost his cool and spoke sharply to the clerk, then apologised and asked for a corrected invoice.
examples.zh: 帳單再次出錯後，顧客失去冷靜，語氣尖銳地對文員說話；之後他道歉，並要求更正發票。

takeaways.en: She was losing her cool when her voice became sharp.
takeaways.zh: 她語氣變得尖銳時，正開始失去冷靜。

takeaways.en: I lost my cool briefly, then paused before answering.
takeaways.zh: 我短暫失去冷靜，然後停一停才回答。
